desc: Understand the sliding window suffix approach: for each right endpoint r, sum mins/maxes over all suffixes of window [max(0, r-k+1), r].
Maintain two deques (min and max) where front corresponds to the oldest suffix, values are monotonic, and each entry stores (value, count).
On right-extension, pop from back while back value is worse than v, merge counts, update running total_min/total_max.
On left-shrink when r-l+1 > k, decrement front count of each deque, subtract from running total, pop if count hits 0.
Add total_min + total_max to answer at each r.
Verify correctness on provided examples (k=2 examples) and edge cases (k=1, all equal elements, k=n).
Run additional random brute-force tests for small n to confirm correctness across diverse inputs.
Double-check the shrinking logic to ensure the deques always represent exactly the suffixes of the current window [l, r].
Ensure integer overflow is not a concern (Python) and confirm final code formatting.
